item.title: Cricket Australia gives players six weeks to share accounts of 2018 ball-tampering scandal
item.description: Cricket Australia (CA) has made public the terms of reference for its independent forum examining the events surrounding the controversial 2018 South Africa tour, which became infamous for the ball-tampering scandal. The six-week exercise will give players and support staff who were part of the tour an opportunity to share their experiences, although individual accounts will remain confidential and will not be made available to the CA Board. The board will instead receive a report summarising the key issues raised during the process, along with recommendations. The document will not include individual testimonies or any supporting material. CA has also committed to releasing the complete report, together with its response, within 30 days of receiving it. The independent exercise will be overseen by senior counsel Fiona McLeod AO SC, who will conduct private sessions with those willing to participate. The forum was announced following fresh revelations surrounding the 2018 scandal in Usman Khawaja's autobiography, Sabr . In the book, Khawaja claimed that awareness of the sandpaper plan extended beyond the three players who were sanctioned by CA. David Warner and Cameron Bancroft have supported parts of his account, while Pat Cummins and several other bowlers have maintained that they had no knowledge of the plan. The forum will examine Australia's ball-management practices during the 2017-18 season, the team's involvement in all four Tests of the South Africa tour, and the incident involving Bancroft during the third Test in Cape Town on March 24, 2018. It will also look into CA's subsequent investigation into the episode. However, the exercise is not intended to reopen the original investigation or establish individual responsibility for the incident. CA has extended invitations to all players and support staff who were part of the South Africa tour, along with the management officials and board directors who were associated with the organisation at the time. Participants will be able to share their accounts through face-to-face or online meetings with McLeod, submit written statements or provide relevant documents. Taking part in the process is voluntary, and those who choose to participate will be permitted to have a support person or legal representative present. The terms of reference also lay down safeguards to protect the confidentiality of participants. Information shared by one individual cannot be attributed to them when seeking clarification from another participant unless they provide consent. Those involved will be informed about who can access their submissions and will have the opportunity to verify their own accounts for accuracy. In addition, the forum will be given access to the 2018 Culture and Governance Review of Australian Cricket conducted by The Ethics Centre, along with other relevant records and documents it considers necessary. item.title: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.”
item.description: Hoffenheim’s squad depth shines in Europa League comeback: “We’re just a really awesome crew.” The strength of Hoffenheim’s bench proved decisive in Thursday evening’s 3-1 Europa League comeback victory over Sturm Graz. Christian Ilzer’s substitutes supplied two of the three goals as the Kraichgauer recovered from a disappointing first half to secure an important European victory against their head coach’s former club. Hoffenheim entered the dressing room trailing 1-0 after Oumar Diakité’s 43rd-minute opener, with sections of the home crowd expressing their displeasure at the halftime whistle. The hosts nevertheless emerged with renewed energy and eventually turned the match around. Speaking to journalists in the mixed zone afterward, Austrian international Alexander Prass insisted that Hoffenheim’s response had not surprised him. “No it doesn’t surprise me,” Prass remarked in the mixed zone when questioned about the comeback. “Because we’re just a really awesome crew. We’re capable of banding together even after a total shit first half, or a not so good first half. Sorry. We can up the energy. Every individual can help us mutually bring what was lacking in the first half. We did everything better in the second half.” Hoffenheim’s substitutes deliver decisive contributions Ilzer’s decision to introduce Patrick Wimmer, Andrej Kramaric, and Bambasé Conté shortly after the hour mark proved particularly influential. Adam Hlozek equalized in the 72nd minute before Conté completed the turnaround eight minutes later, finishing off a Tim Lemperle cross. Substitute Max Moerstedt sealed the 3-1 victory with his first touch in the 90th minute. Wimmer initiated the attack by winning possession, with Kramaric subsequently setting up the young German striker. Conté, himself one of the decisive substitutes, agreed when asked about the quality of Hoffenheim’s options from the bench. “Yeah you could say that,” Conté responded in the mixed zone. “We made it difficult for ourselves in the first half. From the restart onwards we produced a very positive energy with the substitutions and we turned the game around.” Hoffenheim have already benefited from influential substitute appearances this season. As GGFN examined following the club’s 3-0 Bundesliga victory over Bayer Leverkusen , Kramaric also transformed that encounter after entering in the second half, contributing a goal and an assist. Despite Thursday’s successful turnaround, team captain Oliver Baumann was less inclined to celebrate the performance unreservedly. Speaking to RTL after the match, the goalkeeper criticized Hoffenheim’s first-half approach and stressed that the team must learn to sustain its improved football over 70 or 80 minutes rather than relying on one good half. Baumann acknowledged that Hoffenheim remain in a developmental phase. item.description: A referee has hit back at claims he was “drunk” while officiating an AFC Champions League Two match. Footage has been widely shared on social media of Syrian referee Hanna Hattab looking visibly disoriented during a match between Iran 's Gol Gohar and Al Jazira of the United Arab Emirates . One particular incident raised eyebrows when Hattab showed a yellow card to Al Jazira’s goalkeeper for a foul that happened close to the halfway line, 40 yards away from him. Hattab was then replaced at half-time with the fourth official taking over for the remainder of the game, which Al Jazira won 1-0. Reports claimed Gol Gohar staff accused the referee of being drunk following erratic decision-making as similar accusations flooded in online. But Hattab, who is part of the AFC's elite refereeing group, has refuted the allegations as “insult and defamation”, threatening legal action. He wrote in a statement on Facebook: “I confirm that family and personal life are not the responsibility of others, and are not a game in your hands. Religion, reason, and morals do not tolerate the insult of people's privacy or defamation of them. “I also confirm my full right to take all legal and judicial measures against anyone who published or made a statement or contributed to the insult and defamation of me, regardless of their position or status, whether they are an individual, an institution, or a sports entity.” He also said he would issue a further statement following contact with the Syrian Arab Football Federation (SFA) which will “clarify all the details and facts related to what happened ... with full transparency and clarity.” Omani journalist Issa Said, who covers Asian football, has since claimed on social media that what happened to Hattab was "due to a drop in his blood sugar, which caused him to lose concentration and focus". The SFA have also put out a statement standing in support of Hattab, while stating it has requested his medical report from the match. “The Main Referees Committee of the Syrian Arab Football Federation confirms that it stands in full support of international referee Mr Hana Khattab regarding the incident he was subjected to, following reassurance about his health,” it said. “This comes after the committee was reassured of his well-being, following a number of discussions on social media concerning the incident. item.title: Shaquille O’Neal thinks Anthony Edwards can ruin Timberwolves if he fails to notice one thing
item.description: Credit: Marcin Golba/NurPhoto/David Berding via Getty Images The Minnesota Timberwolves have been doing quite well even without Anthony Edwards, and Shaquille O’Neal has sent the superstar a warning about his eventual return. Anthony Edwards has been out indefinitely since he had arthroscopic surgery on his right knee late in October. The Minnesota Timberwolves superstar has missed the entirety of November, and will likely miss all of December and a fair amount of time in January as well. The Timberwolves haven’t struggled all that much in his absence, either. LaMelo Ball has fit the team like a glove, and they have a 14-5 record going into Friday’s game against the Memphis Grizzlies. With that in mind, Shaquille O’Neal recently shared some advice for the young superstar for when he does return. Shaquille O’Neal says Anthony Edwards will have to ensure he doesn’t disrupt team rhythm after returning The Timberwolves have played excellent team ball in Edwards’ absence. He was averaging over 33 points per game in his four games this season. Since he’s been out, though, the team has five players averaging between 12 points to 19 points per game. No one star has been dominating, and this style has been working quite well. So Shaq thinks Edwards will have to be careful with that when he does come back. “I think it’s going to be up to Anthony Edwards,” O’Neal said. “Because right now, he has to see how the guys are playing. Because they’re only playing like this because they’re eating. See, a lot of time when he has the ball, they’re just sitting in the corner, and they’re really out of rhythm. “Now that he’s not there, LaMelo’s kicking it to a damn rhythm. So he has to see this. So when he gets back, he’s going to have to get his and keep his guys in rhythm.” The likes of Jaden McDaniels, Ayo Dosunmu, and Jonathan Kuminga are beginning to truly establish themselves within the context of the team. If Edwards can come back and figure out a seamless fit, no team will want to face off against the Timberwolves in the playoffs this season. item.title: Bayern rule out fine for Kimmich after public criticism over Musiala handling
item.description: Bayern rule out fine for Kimmich after public criticism over Musiala handling Joshua Kimmich made headlines earlier this week after publicly criticising the Bayern Munich hierarchy over their comments on Jamal Musiala's neurological condition and the possibility of adjusting his salary. His comments subsequently sparked speculation over whether he could face disciplinary action, potentially in the form of a fine. However, Bayern sporting director Christoph Freund has now made it clear that no such punishment is being considered. “We never discussed that, and imposing a fine was never a topic of conversation. We're really looking forward and focusing on the upcoming games,” Freund said at Friday's press conference. Sitting alongside Freund, head coach Vincent Kompany was also asked about the vice-captain's outspoken comments but declined to elaborate. Instead, he emphasised that internal matters should remain behind closed doors. “I understand what this question is getting at. However, I can't help you any further with these matters at the moment. We have our bubble, and that's how it will stay," Kompany said. “That doesn't mean we simply applaud everything internally. We tell each other the truth and openly address what hasn't gone well. But I protect these matters, and I lead by example in that regard. “If I were to comment on other issues now, I wouldn't be living up to that standard. My priority is the game against Hamburg.”

item.title: Barcelona injury crisis raises alarm across men’s and women’s teams and Barça Atlètic
item.description: Barcelona injury crisis raises alarm across men’s and women’s teams and Barça Atlètic Barcelona are facing growing concern over an injury crisis affecting several sections of the club, with the men’s and women’s first teams, Barça Atlètic and even the basketball side all struggling with player absences, according to a report from SPORT . The mounting problems have intensified fears that an increasingly congested calendar is taking a physical toll on the club’s athletes across all the divisions. Despite investment in medical staff, rehabilitation support and injury prevention, Barcelona have yet to find a solution to the growing number of setbacks. The situation is particularly troubling for the football department, where Hansi Flick’s first team has repeatedly been forced to manage injuries during demanding stretches of the season. Unfortunately, however, the concern is not limited to the senior squad, with the reserve team also experiencing a difficult run. A packed calendar is testing Barcelona’s prevention work Hansi Flick strengthened the first-team physical preparation staff in July by bringing in Benjamin Kugel , aiming to improve conditioning and reduce late-season injury problems. Hansi Flick has been dealing with player shortages, especially in defence, this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) Yet muscle injuries remain a recurring issue amid international travel and matches every three or four days. Specifically, the stretch involving Betis, Paris Saint-Germain and Real Madrid illustrated the cost. Eric García, Jules Kounde, Xavi Espart and Dani Olmo suffered injuries during that period, while Gerard Martin also experienced discomfort . The sequence left Flick managing absences during a demanding run of fixtures. Barça Atlètic faces the most severe shortage The reserve team has been hit especially hard. Before facing Girona B, Juliano Belletti was dealing with a shortage caused by injuries and international call-ups, with reports counting more than 20 unavailable players. Barcelona requested that the fixture be postponed, but it went ahead. Barcelona have suffered several injuries this season. (Photo by David Ramos/Getty Images) The match brought further damage, as Dani Avila and Ibrahim Diarra were injured , while other players finished with physical problems. Barça Atlètic subsequently lost Mirza Catovic in the derby against Espanyol B. Barcelona confirmed that Catovic had suffered a fibula fracture and would be out for around four months, taking the reserve side’s injury list to 12. Unfortunately, Barcelona’s women’s side is also dealing with a difficult injury situation, while the basketball team has been managing absences during a packed domestic and EuroLeague schedule. The pattern across several departments makes the issue bigger than an isolated run of bad luck. Barcelona have invested in prevention and recovery, but workload, travel and limited rest continue to challenge those measures.

item.title: How Milan winger Moreira infuriated Olympiacos fans and players after Europa League goal
item.description: How Milan winger Moreira infuriated Olympiacos fans and players after Europa League goal Milan winger Diego Moreira infuriated Olympiacos fans and players with his goal celebration in a Europa League game in Athens, prompting Rossoneri coach Ruben Amorim to apologise at full time. The incident happened in the final minutes of the game, after the Belgian winger scored to make it 4-2 for the Rossoneri. PIRAEUS, GREECE – NOVEMBER 26: Gelson Martins of Olympiacos FC is put under pressure from Diego Moreira of AC Milan during the UEFA Europa League 2026/27 League Phase MD5 match between Olympiacos FC and AC Milan at Stadio Georgios Karaiskakis on November 26, 2026 in Piraeus, Greece. (Photo by Milos Bicanski/Getty Images) La Gazzetta dello Sport describes what Moreira did to irritate the home fans and players. The Belgian scored in front of the Greek supporters’ stand and stared at it, motionless, for a few seconds. Safe to say that neither the home fans nor their players enjoyed the celebration, as Manolis Saliakas and João Silva confronted the Milan winger. ITALY – OCTOBER 31: Diego Moreira of AC Milan celebrates scoring his team’s third goal during the Serie A match between AC Milan and FC Internazionale at Stadio Giuseppe Meazza on October 31, 2026 in Italy. (Photo by Marco Luzzani/Getty Images) Silva wagged his finger at him, as to say: ‘You don’t do that in our house.’ A few seconds of tension followed. With Saliakas, there was a grim face-to-face that lasted a few seconds. “It won’t happen again. Moreira is a young lad who plays, but he has to grow,” Milan coach Amorim said at full time. ITALY – NOVEMBER 8: Ruben Amorim, head coach of Milan, looks on prior to kick-off in the Serie A match between Genoa CFC and AC Milan at Stadio Luigi Ferraris on November 8, 2026 in Genoa, Italy. (Photo by Simone Arveda/Getty Images) “We know we wouldn’t like it if they did that to our fans. It’s my responsibility, and I apologise, but he didn’t do it with bad intent.” Moreira has now scored five goals in 12 appearances across all competitions with Milan.

item.title: Fabio Cannavaro reveals Liverpool star Virgil van Dijk's desire to play in Serie A amid AC Milan links
item.description: 버질 판데이크 (Virgil van Dijk) - Getty Images Fabio Cannavaro has revealed that Liverpool centre-back Virgil van Dijk expressed a desire to play in Serie A during a conversation at the World Cup. With the Dutchman's contract expiring in June 2027, the Italy legend believes a switch to AC Milan would be an exciting move. Van Dijk eyes Italian football adventure Liverpool could face a battle to keep hold of Van Dijk as speculation grows over his long-term future . The Dutch centre-back has reportedly emerged on Milan's radar ahead of next season. Former Italy international Cannavaro has now added fuel to those rumours in an interview with Gazzetta dello Sport . The 2006 Ballon d'Or winner disclosed that Van Dijk is genuinely intrigued by the prospect of testing himself in Italian football. Van Dijk existing deal with Liverpool is set to expire in June 2027, leaving the door open for potential suitors to monitor his availability. Cannavaro backs Dutchman for Milan switch Cannavaro explained that his insight came directly from a personal conversation with the Liverpool defender during the World Cup. Having represented Napoli, Parma, Juventus, and Inter during his own career, the Italian icon believes Milan would be a fitting destination. "I saw him at the World Cup and he told me that he would like to have an experience in Italy," Cannavaro said. "He is very fascinated by it. It would be nice to see Van Dijk at Milan." Physical dominance and the Maldini comparison While Cannavaro is clearly an admirer of Van Dijk's attributes, he also offered a candid tactical assessment of how elite defenders evolve over time. Drawing on his own experiences and an anecdote involving Paolo Maldini, Cannavaro highlighted the vital role of pace in defending. "In recent years, he has combined great physical strength with outstanding speed," Cannavaro noted. "Once, a coach said to Paolo Maldini: 'You turn badly.' And he replied: 'Mister, as long as I get to the ball.'" Cannavaro warned that relying on recovery speed comes with an inevitable caveat later in a player's career. "It was the same for me," he added. "When you are very fast, you can afford a technical error. The problem comes when that speed is no longer there." What next for Van Dijk's future? With Van Dijk's Liverpool contract running until June 2027, the club still hold a strong position regarding his immediate future. However, Milan's reported interest for next season means the Italian side could soon test Liverpool's resolve. Whether Van Dijk decides to act on his fascination with Serie A remains to be seen.

item.title: Botman banned from driving for using phone at wheel
item.description: Newcastle United defender Sven Botman has been banned from driving [PA] Premier League footballer Sven Botman has been banned from driving after being caught using his mobile phone at the wheel. The Newcastle United centre-back pleaded guilty to using a handheld mobile phone while using a motor vehicle on a road at Newcastle Magistrates' Court on Wednesday. The 26-year-old was given six penalty points and disqualified from driving for six months, as these were added to points he had already accrued. He was fined £900 and ordered to pay £400 costs and a £360 victim surcharge, the MoJ said. Botman was driving a Land Rover on the A189 Haddricks Mill Road, in Newcastle, on 17 September when he was spotted using his phone. The Dutchman changed his plea from not guilty to guilty at his court appearance on Wednesday, the MoJ confirmed. Newcastle United signed Botman from Lille in 2022. item.title: Clashes mar European games as Macron condemns violence
item.description: Fan violence marred the tie at the Stade Velodrome [Getty Images] Violent clashes marred a number of European football matches on Thursday night, with French president Emmanuel Macron condemning trouble at Marseille's home game against Levski Sofia. There were also incidents at games between Turkish side Besiktas and Israel's Hapoel Be'er-Sheva in Georgia and Sunderland's 1-1 home draw with Poland's Jagiellonia Bialystok. In Marseille, the build-up to the Europa League match at the Stade Velodrome was affected by incidents in the stands, including the throwing of projectiles and flares between the two sets of supporters. With 10 minutes to go until kick-off, several Marseille fans ran from a home stand, appearing to pursue a group of Levski Sofia supporters. They breached the stand designated for away fans, which housed around 500 supporters of the Bulgarian domestic champions. "Five people were taken to hospital with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder," said the Marseille police prefecture. "Six others were treated on site for various wounds." Macron spoke to Bulgarian Prime Minister Rumen Radev about the incidents, with the French president condemning "with the utmost force these acts of violence, which have no place in sport or in public space", and reassured him that "these acts would not go unpunished". According to news agency Reuters, Radev thanked Macron for his personal involvement following the "attack on Bulgarian citizens" and for the medical assistance provided to the victims. Bulgarian President Iliana Iotova said she found video footage of the incidents "shocking" in a statement posted on social media. "The attacks against the Bulgarian fans desecrate one of the great games that brings millions of people together around the world," she added. "Everyone should be able to support their team without being afraid for their safety." The police source said all the people injured were Bulgarian and there was "no information at this stage regarding any arrests". Security personnel managed to restore calm, allowing the game to kick-off on time, although there were a few further flare-ups between the fans, notably during the half-time break in a match Marseille won 1-0. "It's a very regrettable episode. item.description: Photo by David Cannon/Getty Images LIV Golf officially applied for bankruptcy and began the process of going into liquidation earlier this month. Their plans for a new version of the league – LIV 2.0 – failed to get off the ground after they failed to get enough players to sign up to the project. After many years of bullish promises, LIV Golf is finally finished and the fallout from their collapse will be ongoing for quite some time. LIV Golf may have made a lot of big-name players incredibly wealthy initially, but a lot of golfers have been left in the lurch over the past 12 months regarding payments they’re due. However, it is tough to extract money from a business that has entered into bankruptcy. One golfer in particular is claiming that he is owed a lot of money from the former Saudi-backed league. Lucas Herbert claims he’s ‘owed a lot’ of money from LIV Golf The talented Lucas Herbert spoke with Fox Sports Australia about his recent exit from LIV Golf. The 30-year-old Australian claimed he’s still owed a lot of money from LIV, but suggested that he doesn’t regret his decision to join the league in the first place. “ You’re probably foolish to think you’re going to get much of it. Anything from this point is going to be a bonus, “ Herbert said. “ It’s a long drawn out process with mostly lawyers winning out of the whole battle. I’ve accepted that and moved on. The reality is I made a lot of money at the same time as I’m owed a lot. “ As great as a time I had on the LIV tour, I had many legal issues along the way, which drew a lot of energy out of me. I’ve played this game a few times now and I’m going to expect not very much and hopefully be pleasantly surprised, rather than the other way around. “ I’ve got no problem saying we were poorly communicated with as players throughout the season,” he said. “ A lot of times mainstream media, or media outlets outside of LIV, knew more about what was going on than we did, which was pretty tough to deal with. It was a bit of a contributing factor as to why very few guys were interested in going around again in 2.0. “ It was a tough off-season to have everyone having an opinion on what your livelihood and career and future looks like when you don’t have control over (it) yourself. It’s one thing for people to have their opinions on your poor play, but it felt people at times took pride in seeing everything we tried to build at LIV fail. “ I’m still very happy with the decision I made – it doesn’t look like I’m in a great position right now, but time will tell. “ Herbert is a sensational golfer, so he will undoubtedly make millions of dollars in the future. However, the fact that he is owed so much money from LIV Golf must really be eating away at him. No wonder none of the big names were keen to sign up to LIV 2.0 after being treated so poorly.

item.title: Ex-Man United ace Alejandro Garnacho left staring into the abyss after Aston Villa decision
item.description: Ex-Man United ace Alejandro Garnacho left staring into the abyss after Aston Villa decision Former Manchester United forward Alejandro Garnacho has plunged to a new all-time low, with Aston Villa making a major decision on his future ahead of the January transfer window. Troubles Garnacho was nowhere to be seen on Tuesday evening as Villa suffered a 1-0 Champions League defeat to Galatasaray. Villa boss Unai Emery opted to name 11 substitutes instead of the allowed 12. Emery took the decision amid deepening concerns over the trajectory of Garnacho ‘s career. Since his £40m move from United to Chelsea in the summer of 2025, he has endured a torrid time, having departed after falling out with then-manager Ruben Amorim. He struggled both for form and consistency at Chelsea, managing just one Premier League goal all term. Chelsea decided they had seen enough and approved a move to Villa , initially on loan, with the deal set to become an obligation depending on appearances. But Garnacho has so far failed to impress Emery, both during games and on the training pitch. The Argentine has been omitted from the previous two Premier League squads and has accumulated only 34 minutes of top-flight football. He has made just seven appearances from the bench. According to The Athletic , Villa are actively working to offload the Carrington academy graduate in January. New low The Athletic reports, “Two Villa sources stated in October that they would be amazed if Garnacho did not end up their player beyond the season, with staff being briefed that the initial loan came with the extreme likelihood that Garnacho would transition into a permanent acquisition.” Alejandro Garnacho 2026/27 record Aston Villa · 2026/27 “Garnacho had wanted to leave England before meeting with Emery, who convinced him to stay. But Garnacho has failed to make an impact in Villa’s first-team environment, with performances in training not doing enough to suggest he deserves a chance to play regularly.” “Multiple sources have said Villa are open to his departure in January, provided clubs from overseas come to the table and strike an agreement with his parent club, Chelsea.” It’s understood to be unknown whether Chelsea would want Garnacho, having already considered his exit sealed. Thank you.” We Made #H1STORY 🔴🏆 #ForzaDucati #ValenciaGP pic.twitter.com/Y0lW7ZAshJ — Ducati Corse (@ducaticorse) November 27, 2026 Marquez captured the MotoGP title last weekend in Portugal to go level with the great Giacomo Agostini on a record eight premier-class championships. He soaked in the glory in Lisbon, marking the occasion by ascending the staircase accompanied by the silhouette of a goat on the screen, a nod to his growing “Greatest of All ⁠Time” status, before receiving a golden commemorative helmet from Agostini himself. There were tears in the Ducati garage as well as in the stands when fans were told the Spaniard would be competing in his final race this weekend at ‌the Circuit Ricardo Tormo. Marc Marquez celebrates his eighth MotoGP title win (Reuters) "Thank you to everyone ​who's ⁠been part of the journey. I hope you've enjoyed it as ⁠much as I have. This will be ​my ⁠last race in MotoGP. ‌We made history," Marquez said in a video statement in the garage in ‌Valencia. Marquez won six titles with Honda in the space of seven years before making the switch to Ducati, with whom he has claimed back-to-back championships in the last two years. He had initially extended his contract with the Italian outfit until 2028 in June, but has now opted to call time on his legendary career. His title success this year came despite undergoing double surgery midway through the season on his right shoulder. Marquez has retired from MotoGP (Reuters) “I know that we are here celebrating a historic moment. I know how I suffered," said an emotional ⁠Marquez after the Portuguese Grand Prix. "I know that in the middle of the season, the fans believed more than I did. My people believed more than I did. But I kept pushing, I kept doing my best. item.title: Levski Sofia fans hospitalised after violent clashes with Marseille supporters
item.description: Marseille head coach Bruno Genesio said “we are living through violent times” after five Levski Sofia fans were hospitalised following violent clashes before their Europa League encounter with the French side. Groups of supporters threw projectiles and flares and French outlet L’Equipe reported that there were Nazi salutes observed in the away section. Ten minutes before kick-off at the Stade Velodrome a group of Marseille fans broke through into the away stand, which housed around 500 fans. In the ensuing clashes five people, all Bulgarian, were injured and taken to hospital “with eye injuries, head trauma and a dislocated shoulder”, according to the Marseille police prefecture, while six others were treated on-site for more superficial injuries. The police force said there was “no information at this stage regarding any arrests”. Security were able to restore order and the game kicked off on time, although there were further incidents later on, particularly at half-time. Genesio said: “We are living through violent times in our society, so this is very, very regrettable.” Julio Velazquez, head coach of the Bulgarian domestic champions, said: “It's a very regrettable episode. These are incidents which are unacceptable for football.” The Bulgarian Football Union condemned the violence and said it had referred the incident to UEFA , calling for the harshest possible sanctions. It also demanded full cooperation and transparency from French authorities in investigating the attacks and identifying those responsible. There were violent clashes before kick-off (Reuters) Levski said the club's priority is the safety and well-being of its fans. A statement read: “What happened tonight is particularly alarming given the extraordinary security measures put in place by the French authorities, as well as the restrictions imposed on our travelling supporters—restrictions that the club had already formally contested with UEFA. “Despite the risks identified by the club prior to the match, the measures taken failed to provide adequate protection for our fans. This is completely unacceptable.” Both clubs condemned the violence (Reuters) Marseille also condemned the violence and said it is conducting “a thorough analysis of the circumstances in which these incidents took place.” Bulgarian President Iliana Yotova called for those responsible to be held accountable and Prime Minister Rumen Radev said he had spoken to French president Emmanuel Macron about the violence at a European summit in Brussels. A spokesperson for Macron’s office said: “He condemned in the strongest possible terms these acts of violence targeting Bulgarian supporters, which have no place in sport or in public spaces, and assured the Prime Minister that these acts would not go unpunished.” Marseille won the game 1-0, with Amine Gouiri scoring a 28th-minute penalty.

item.title: Tyson Fury's wife backtracks on schizophrenia claim
item.description: British heavyweight boxer Tyson Fury faces Anthony Joshua in Cardiff on December 11 (Fayez Nureldine) Paris Fury, the wife of Tyson Fury, has retracted her claim that the British heavyweight was diagnosed with schizophrenia just months after he was crowned world champion in 2015. In clips promoting a Netflix documentary, the boxer spoke about his mental health struggles following his victory over Ukraine's Wladimir Klitschko in Germany. Paris Fury said Tyson Fury had "mild schizophrenia" in an initial version of the documentary, which will be released on Friday. Netflix said it had worked to "update" the footage in light of her clarification. Fury, 38, is due to face Anthony Joshua in a long-awaited all-British showdown in Cardiff on December 11. Paris Fury's comments come after the British Boxing Board of Control indicated that it was investigating the comments, though Robert Smith, the board's general secretary, told the BBC it was "fairly confident" he would be cleared to fight Joshua. "I want to clarify a statement I made in the original version of the Tyson Fury documentary," Paris said in a statement. "I recalled a conversation from many years ago when discussing Tyson's condition and I used the word 'schizophrenic'. Whilst Tyson did show some symptoms associated with schizophrenia, he doesn't have this condition and has never received a diagnosis. "Mental health is complex, and it isn't always easy to find the right words, especially when you're living it with someone you love. "I'm so proud of Tyson for really opening up in this documentary and want to say thank you for all the support we've received as a family." Fury has been open about his mental health struggles since beating Klitschko, after which he took a break of nearly three years from boxing. His weight ballooned while he battled suicidal thoughts and drug and alcohol problems. Fury admitted hearing "voices in my mind" following his win, adding: "Words can't explain the darkness I was in. "I came from the living version of the pits of hellfire. And I 100 percent thought at times I'd end up in a padded room with the door locked, and that scared me so much." Fury became world heavyweight champion for a second time when he beat WBC champion Deontay Wilder in February 2020. Despite losing twice to Oleksandr Usyk in 2024, the only losses in his 39-fight professional career, Fury could become a three-time world champion when he takes on Joshua with the vacant WBA title set to be on the line. Netflix said in a statement: "Following new information shared by the family relating to Tyson's official mental health diagnosis, we have worked alongside them to update the documentary accordingly ahead of launch." jw/jkb/td

item.title: Michael Olise ruled out of Bayern's trip to Hamburg
item.description: Michael Olise ruled out of Bayern's trip to Hamburg Bayern Munich head coach Vincent Kompany has confirmed that Michael Olise will miss Saturday's Bundesliga clash with Hamburger SV. The French winger also sat out Wednesday's 2-1 Champions League defeat to LOSC Lille after suffering a bruised foot in last week's 1-1 draw with 1. FC Köln. “Michael [Olise] won't play,” Kompany confirmed at a press conference on Friday. "Everything else is open. The priority is the team, not individual players. We've got four games - including Wednesday - in nine days. We need to use our squad - and it is how it is at the moment. Everything's open, but we still have the same demands." In addition to Olise, Bayern will also be without Harry Kane, Ismaël Saibari, Serge Gnabry, Alphonso Davies and Manuel Neuer due to injury. “The reality is that we're missing 130 goals in the squad. But we still have the same demands. We want to win. We didn't do that, which doesn't feel good. At the moment we only have one superstar, which is the team. My focus is on this superstar,” Kompany said. On the positive side, Kompany believes Bayern's current injury crisis presents an opportunity for young, unproven players such as Noah Codjo-Evora and Tim Binder to step up, make their mark and gain valuable first-team experience. “What can this period mean for a club? We can give two or three players some experience who could prove vital at the end of the season. That can’t happen if the guys don’t get the playing time they need. We’ve still factored them into our plans in this situation. We know that something like what we’re currently experiencing can always happen. That’s why their role will very quickly become very important,” Kompany said. "[Noah] Codjo-Evora has often been injured, but he’s a very well-rounded player. He’s very precise with his first touch, is ambidextrous, can finish, and has strength. You can see where he’s capable of going in the future. Tim Binder is quick in one-v-one situations. They’ve been training with us for a long time now, but they all still need to develop. "However, we hope they can play without pressure. If they don’t perform well now, it doesn’t mean it’s all over. They’re young players who are helping us and who might be able to help us even more at the end of the season, because they’re gaining experience now."

item.title: Marc Marquez to end storied MotoGP career after eighth world crown
item.description: Marc Marquez won his eighth MotoGP title last weekend (FILIPE AMORIM) Marc Marquez will bring the curtain down on his MotoGP career after this weekend's season-ending Grand Prix in Valencia, following a historic season in which he won his record-equalling eighth title. Spaniard Marquez claimed his eighth title in the premier class of motorcycling last weekend at the Portuguese Grand Prix, his second in as many years for Italian team Ducati. "It is official. @marcmarquez93 has decided to retire from @motogp, and the 2026 Valencia Grand Prix will be his final race as a professional rider and with the #DucatiLenovoTeam," said Ducati on social media on Friday. Marquez then relayed his own message, via a video recorded on the paddock at the Ricardo Tormo circuit, with a series of placards held up to the camera. "Thank you to everyone who's been part of this journey, I hope you've enjoyed it as much as I have," said Marquez. "This will be my last race in MotoGP. We made history." Marquez's latest success pulled him level with Italian great Giacomo Agostini who won his titles between 1966 and 1975. He also overtakes his great rival Valentino Rossi, who won seven MotoGP titles, although the swashbuckling Italian has 89 individual race wins in the top category to Marquez's 80. The latest triumph is even more remarkable given the 33-year-old's injury and crash-blighted campaign in which he had to wait until the eighth race in Hungary on June 7 before claiming his first win. Marquez suffered a flat tyre in the season-opener in Thailand in March, fell at the Spanish GP in Jerez and again at the French GP where he picked up a foot fracture which ruled him out of the following race, the Catalan GP. Making his comeback at the Italian GP in Mugello he trailed Bezzecchi by a massive 102 points in early June just weeks after undergoing foot surgery on top of a previous operation on his injured shoulder. But once he got rolling he roared into a regular winning run with seven Grand Prix and 10 sprint race victories in all this season. td/ach

item.title: Real Madrid defender not thinking about January exit despite uncertain future – report
item.description: Real Madrid defender not thinking about January exit despite uncertain future – report Among all the signings Real Madrid have made in the recent past, Trent Alexander-Arnold has perhaps been the most disappointing one. The Englishman came in with the reputation of being one of the world’s best right-backs, having won the Champions League and the Premier League at Liverpool. But 18 months into his Real Madrid career, the defender has yet to establish himself as a first-team regular at the club, even after the summer exit of Dani Carvajal. This has led to question marks over Trent’s future, with Chelsea and Manchester United among the clubs interested in his services. Trent not thinking about an exit Trent has fallen behind Federico Valverde in the pecking order. (Photo by Denis Doyle/Getty Images) However, a recent report from The Athletic has indicated that Trent is not thinking about leaving Real Madrid in the upcoming January transfer window. The English international is not too keen on leaving Santiago Bernabeu just 18 months after joining the club and is trying to do everything he can to establish himself as a first-team starter. This comes against the backdrop of calls for Trent to return to Liverpool, with club legend Steven Gerrard endorsing the idea recently. But it appears the right-back has no desire to give up just yet and wants to fight for his place in the starting eleven. Can Trent become a starter at Real Madrid? Trent’s future at Real Madrid looks uncertain. (Photo by Angel Martinez/Getty Images) It is clear that Jose Mourinho has liked what he has seen from Federico Valverde and considers the Uruguayan international his first-choice right-back this season. As for Trent, he has struggled to perform even when given limited opportunities, with the Englishman most recently failing to make an impression against Celta Vigo. This doesn’t bode well for Trent’s chances, especially given the fact that he also has competition from Denzel Dumfries. However, the month of December could be interesting for Mourinho, who has embraced more rotations in recent weeks in an attempt to keep his first-choice players fit and healthy for the important matches. Between now and Christmas, Real Madrid are slated to play six matches, and it won’t be surprising to see Trent appear in at least a few of them, which in turn, could be his opportunity to impress Mourinho, heading into the second half of the season.

item.description: George Russell has claimed that few other Formula 1 drivers would have attempted the same move as Max Verstappen during their controversial practice encounter at the Las Vegas Grand Prix , insisting that his reaction would have been identical regardless of who was behind the wheel. The two drivers reignited their long-standing rivalry in Las Vegas after making contact during the final practice session while preparing for their respective flying laps. The incident resulted in a five-place grid penalty for Verstappen, although the Dutchman subsequently inherited pole position following Kimi Antonelli's own grid penalty. Russell addressed those remarks upon arriving in Qatar, describing Verstappen's comments as unnecessary. item.title: Wanderers approved for home stadium leasehold
item.description: The Wanderers have played at Meadowbank since 2018, after it was refurbished [Getty Images] The proposed transfer of ownership of Meadowbank Stadium from Surrey County Football Association to Dorking Wanderers Football Club has been approved by Mole Valley District Council. The Wanderers have played there since 2018 after it was refurbished. It had previously been home to Dorking FC prior to their disbanding. The club said it "marks a significant milestone" following several years of hard work to reach this point. Completion of the lease arrangements remains subject to approval from the East Surrey Shadow Authority executive, according to the district council, due to local government reorganisation in the county. A club spokesperson said: "Taking responsibility for Meadowbank will give the club greater control over its future, creating opportunities to develop additional income streams and build on the stadium's role as a hub for the community." The acquisition is being supported by new co-owners Frank Villares and Debra Tucker. The pair recently bought a stake in the sixth-tier club , which was formed and is owned and managed by Marc White. The club said it has provided the funding necessary to complete the deal. Villares said: "Getting involved in Dorking Wanderers was about several things for Debra and me. "Of course we want to see success on the pitch and we're sure we will, but creating income streams for the club is crucial. "I'd like to thank everyone at Mole Valley District Council and Surrey County Football Association for their cooperation and support throughout this process. "We're looking forward to taking over the operation of Meadowbank and building on what is already a fantastic hub for the community." item.description: Photo by Christian Petersen/Getty Images The Golden State Warriors head coach explained how they’ve made a few changes after realising the team was relying too much on superstar Stephen Curry. When the season began, nobody expected the Golden State Warriors to be competitive this season. However, a stellar start to the season by Stephen Curry and the emergence of Yaxel Lendeborg saw them get off to an 8-4 start. As if things were going too well, though, Curry was struck down by injury. The team has understandably struggled since Curry has been out with an abdominal tear. They have a 2-4 record, averaging just 104.3 points per game in the games he has missed this year. Their last two results have brought back some positivity, though, with wins against the Celtics and the Kings. Head coach Steve Kerr has revealed that he has been working to minimise the effect of not having Steph. Steve Kerr says Warriors realised their offensive dependence on Steph Curry and have ‘tweaked’ the offence to change that If the Warriors can stay competitive, the return of Curry and Jimmy Butler along with a potential trade later in the season could completely change how they are viewed. For that, they must continue to win as much as they can in their superstar’s absence. The Warriors’ problem has always been that their superstars are so unique, that the system tends to fail in their absence. But it seems the coach has identified it this time, as he recently explained. “We’ve recognized that the way we were running our offense was too Steph-dependent, and so we’ve tweaked a few things, and I want to qualify that by saying whatever we run, Steph’s going to score,” Kerr said on the Tom Tolbert Show. “It doesn’t matter what we run for Steph, but it matters for everybody else, and so the way some of the nuances within our offense we needed to tweak, and we’ve made some changes this week, and hopefully we’ll be better for it long term.” After a tough matchup against the Portland Trail Blazers in their next game, the Warriors will face the Clippers and the Jazz in what they should consider to be winnable games. If the tweaks work, maybe they can keep their heads above water and set the stage for Curry’s eventual return to the court, which hopefully isn’t too far off.
